summary: Built a commented Node.js LlamaIndex recommendation agent with DiskANN retrieval, co-purchase reranking, isolated session memory, and repeatable 20,000-order ingestion. Includes configuration validation, documentation, offline tests, and a live verifier. No cloud resources, data, or indexes were changed.
how_to_run: Run npm ci. Copy .env.example to .env in your editor and populate DOCUMENTDB_URI with the portal connection string and OPENAI_API_KEY locally. Against an authorized existing M30+ test cluster, run npm run ingest, then npm start -- sample-p001 alice --interactive. Run npm test and npm run check for offline verification; npm run verify:live checks the seeded database and model integration.
verification_done: npm ci --no-audit: dependency installation from lockfile succeeded.
npm test: 11 passed, including real LlamaIndex workflow execution with a fake streaming model, session isolation, embedding caching, and deterministic 20,000-order generation.
npm run check: syntax checks passed for 13 JavaScript files.
MongoDB-driver connect and ping succeeded using the runner-provided environment URI.
Read-only database checks confirmed the isolated sample database was empty; the co-purchase aggregation returned an empty result and unknown-product handling passed.
not_verified: Live ingestion, embedding generation, DiskANN creation/retrieval, and five-item model recommendations: OPENAI_API_KEY was missing and the sample database was unseeded.
Actual cluster M30+ tier and indexed query performance were not confirmed.
Recommendation quality and ranking weights remain demonstration assumptions, not measured quality results.
Node.js 22 execution was not tested; verification used Node.js 26.13.0.
Detailed dependency security audit failed with HTTP 429 from the package proxy.
open_issues: Installation reported three high-severity dependency findings. Affected-package details and remediation require a successful npm audit before production use.
The audit-trail tool failed twice; subsequent decisions and workarounds were recorded in DECISIONS.md.
